name: Leila Ahmed
shortBio: Egyptian-American historian and philosopher of gender in Islam whose genealogy traced how colonial officials co-opted "feminist" rhetoric ("colonial feminism") to legitimize Western imperial rule while silencing indigenous women's ethical voices.
centralQuestion: How was the discourse of Muslim women's liberation co-opted by Western imperialism, and what ethical egalitarianism endures inside Islamic tradition?

keyWorks.title: Women and Gender in Islam: Historical Roots of a Modern Debate
keyWorks.description: Foundational intellectual history distinguishing Islam's ethical voice from androcentric Abbasid jurisprudence and European "colonial feminism."

keyWorks.title: A Quiet Revolution: The Veil's Resurgence, from the Middle East to America
keyWorks.description: Sociological genealogy of contemporary Muslim women's diverse ethical and civic negotiations of dress and piety.
